(per Hon'ble Sri Justice P.Naveen Rao) Heard Mr. Ravula Sowmya Reddy learned counsel for Shaik Fathima vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 9 February, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106562558/
1 petitioners and the learned Government Pleader appearing for learned Advocate General for Home for respondents.

sentences.text:
2. These three writ petitions are filed challenging the order of detention of the detenues dated 01.06.2021 made in exercise of power under Section 3(2) of the "The Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders,
Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertiliser Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986).

entities.text: Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The orders of detention are confirmed by the Government vide orders dated 18.08.2021, 09.08.2021 and 10.08.2021, respectively.

3. The detaining authority alleges that the detenues were involved in four crimes, i.e., Crime No.103 of 2021 under Section 395 of IPC, Crime No.104 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC of Inthezargunj Police Station, Crime No.113 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC and Crime No.114 of 2021 under Section 394 of IPC of Hasanparthy Police Station.

entities.text: Inthezargunj Police Station, Crime No.113 of 2021
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The detenues were arrested on PNR,J & GRR,J WP Nos.23492 of 2021 & batch 20.04.2021.

According to the learned counsel for detenues, they have moved bail applications in two crimes, i.e., Crime Nos.113 and 114 of 2021 of Hasanparthy Police Station, but in the meantime they were detained.

Because of the preventive detention orders,
they were not granted bail in those two bail applications.

4. By placing reliance on earlier decision rendered by this Court, following the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, learned counsel for the detenues contends that order of detentions are ex facie illegal, the crimes alleged against the detenues do not warrant resorting to extraordinary measure of preventively detaining them as the offences alleged are under IPC and are triable in accordance with Criminal Procedure Code.

He further submits that the detenues are in custody since 20.04.2021 and on account of the orders of detention, their life and liberty is affected for more than nine months and no justification is made, even otherwise, to continue the detention any further.
He would further submit that in any case even if detention order is set aside, they cannot be released unless applications to grant bail are moved and competent Court grants them bail.
5. Learned Government Pleader submits that by indulging in crimes registered against them, the detenues are creating panic situation and fear in general public.
The Police apprehend that if the detenues are released, they would continue to indulge in committing such crimes and would seriously jeopardize public order.
He therefore justifies the orders of detention.
PNR,J & GRR,J WP Nos.23492 of 2021 & batch 6.
The issue need not detain us further having regard to the decision rendered by this Court in W.P.No.16921 of 2021.

In the said case, the order of detention was made by referring to involvement of detenu in five crimes, out of which three crimes relate to theft of two wheeler motorcycles and two crimes relate to theft of cell phones, in addition, in one crime theft of cash was also alleged.
This Court noticed that these are normal law and order crimes, subject to trial before the competent Shaik Fathima vs The State Of Telangana And 2 Others on 9 February, 2022

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Indian
Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106562558/
2 criminal Court and does not require resorting to extraordinary measure of preventive detention.

Taking note of the view expressed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Banka Sneha Sheela Vs. The State of Telangana1, this Court held that crimes registered against the detenu would not lead to harm, danger or alarm or feeling of insecurity among the general public, necessitating resorting to such extraordinary measure.

entities.text: Banka Sneha Sheela Vs. The State of Telangana1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 7. In the instant case also, we are of the opinion that on the crimes alleged against the detenues, it is not necessary to take such extraordinary measure of preventively detaining them.
The crimes alleged against detenues would not lead to harm, danger or alarm or feeling of insecurity among the public at large.
8. For the aforesaid reasons, the orders of detention are not sustainable and are accordingly set aside.
Writ Petitions are allowed.
The respondents are directed to set the detenues, namely, Shaik Gafar s/o.Abbas (W.P.No.23492 of 2021),

Mohd.Feroz @ Babloo s/o.Afzal (W.P.No.23499 of 2021),
and Shaik Rafeeq, s/o.Shabbir (W.P.No.23504 of 2021), at liberty forthwith, if they 2021 SCC Online SC 530 (Crl.A.No.733 of 2021), PNR,J & GRR,J WP Nos.23492 of 2021 & batch are no longer required in any other criminal case.
Pending miscellaneous petitions if any shall stand closed.

_ _ ____ JUSTICE G.RADHA RANI
